description: Capabilities granted to the Karma Yoga window and to the windows opened on a single app (src/windows.rs: the same interface as the main window, so the same grant). Deliberately narrow where it can be: the webview has no network permission at all and its content security policy allows no outbound connection, so nothing it renders -- an entry, a task, an event fetched from a subscribed calendar, or a book cover downloaded into the vault -- can cause a request. Every socket in the application is opened by the Rust shell through src/http.rs, only for a calendar feed the user pasted in or a metadata lookup they asked for, and none of it is reachable from here. The one thing it may ask the shell to open is an https:// link in the system browser -- an OAuth sign-in page, chiefly; opener:allow-open-url carries no scope of its own, and without this one every URL is refused. There is no dialog permission: every picker and confirmation is raised from Rust (src/transfer.rs, src/files.rs, src/guard.rs), where page script cannot answer it, and a dialog the page could raise itself is one it could dress up as the shell's. The allow-* entries are the application's own commands (declared in build.rs, registered in src/lib.rs); this window uses all of them. When one is added to build.rs it has to be added here as well -- `cargo test -p karmayoga-app --lib acl::` checks.
